subject: Late-stage sizing and soft reserve request — ZenithPoint POC
messages:
From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@zenithpoint.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ZenithPoint POC - request for temporary dedicated sizing and soft reserve

Hi Soojin / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the model latency profiles look promising. We're pushing to a production-oriented POC that will include a 10M token/day ingestion window and a mix of short/med sequences for retrieval-augmented generation. Based on our internal forecasts, we'll need a dedicated scheduling window to guarantee consistent latency during the pilot.

Ask: can Redwood place a soft hold on roughly 12 A100-equivalent GPUs (or H100-quantized equivalent) in us-west-2 for the window 2028-11-01 -> 2029-02-28? This would be a standby allocation while we finalize commercial terms (we expect an MSA + SOW within 2 weeks). We are open to a short commitment term and understand there may be a ramp/burst policy.

Attached: workload_profile_v3.csv + tiling_model_profile_v2.xlsx (model sequence mix + expected qps).

Key constraints:
- Hard latency SLO: 95th percentile < 220ms for 8k-context retrieval calls
- Prefix caching will be used for common prompts
- Data residency: processed in us-west-2 only

Next steps: can you confirm current inventory availability and any limitations (node affinity, multi-tenant fallbacks, expected per-token cost delta for a soft hold)? If feasible, please propose a mutual action plan we can include in procurement.

Best,
Alice Gomez
Head of ML Ops, ZenithPoint
Attachment: tiling_model_profile_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), workload_profile_v3.csv (csv)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@zenithpoint.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ZenithPoint POC - request for temporary dedicated sizing and soft reserve

Alice — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. We're aligned that a soft hold makes sense for a late-stage POC to avoid queuing variability.

Quick plan from our side:
- I'll coordinate a soft standby reservation with Capacity/Ops. This is non-binding but will prevent allocation to new multi-tenant bursts.
- Marcus, can you run a cross-region inventory check and confirm whether the target is best served by 12 A100-equivalent or we should recommend H100 quantized variants for cost/latency tradeoffs? Please include a short fallback (8x A100 + 4x burstable nodes) if full 12 cannot be held.
- Karthik — sales will prepare a 14-day MAP (mutual action plan) and an order form that codifies the hold window and pricing uplift for dedicated standby. We should target having that to ZenithPoint by EOD Mon.

Operational notes for ZenithPoint (Alice):
- Soft hold means capacity is earmarked for you but can be reclaimed on 48h notice in extreme fleet stress; we will notify you and offer routing to compatible multi-tenant models as a fallback.
- Billing: standby surcharge applied daily during the hold; actual consumption billed separately per token.

I'll follow up once Marcus posts the snapshot.

— Soojin
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@zenithpoint.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ZenithPoint POC - inventory snapshot + recommendations

Soojin / team — ran an inventory and feasibility check against current scheduled jobs and reservations. Summary:

- us-west-2 current free capacity (A100-equivalent): 9 GPUs immediately available for soft reserve.
- Additional 6 GPUs can be made available by shifting a low-priority training window (estimated reclamation window: 72 hours).
- H100-quantized option: 12 H100-like throughput-equivalents are technically available but require a quantized runtime profile (we'd recommend 8-bit quant + KV cache tuning). Latency delta estimated: +10–18% p95 compared to A100 at same qps, but per-token cost would drop ~22%.

Recommendation:
- Offer ZenithPoint a tiered standby: 9 guaranteed A100-equivalents + conditional 3-node burst (72h reclamation) OR 12 H100-quantized equivalents with the quantization caveat. Given their tight 95p latency target, I'd suggest the mixed approach (9 dedicated A100 + 3 burstable) and an option to switch to quantized variants after initial tuning.

I've uploaded a capacity snapshot to the shared drive and attached a short PDF. If Sales wants to lock a soft hold today we can apply an earmark policy flag to those 9 nodes and schedule the remainder as conditional. Operationally, that would show up as a "standby: earmarked" tag in the console and a daily standby surcharge.

Attachment: capacity_snapshot_us-west-2_20280831.pdf

— Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@zenithpoint.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ZenithPoint POC - next steps and MAP

Alice / Soojin — thanks Marcus for the snapshot. Alice, we can proceed with the mixed standby approach Marcus recommended. Next steps from Sales:

1) I'll send a 14-day Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that ties the soft hold to an MSA signature milestone (target: 2028-09-10).
2) I'll create the HubSpot opportunity and attach the MAP + Marcus's snapshot. (link: https://hubspot.company/record/ZP-2028-092)
3) If you approve the MAP, we'll apply the earmark to 9 A100-equivalents today and flag 3 nodes as conditional burst (72h).

Could you confirm acceptance of the MAP milestones and the billing approach (standby daily surcharge + usage billing)? If yes, I'll mark the internal hold and notify Capacity to apply the earmark.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
